messages:
incident-bot: Paging oncall: detected sustained QPS spike for org=triton-labs, error rate rising from 0.2% -> 2.8% over 5m, latency p95 780ms. Auto-mitigations not sufficient. @oncall-ryan can you take?

oncall-ryan: I'm up. looking at dashboards now — link: https://console.redwood.internal/dashboards/orgs/triton-labs/traffic (charts show 3x baseline). Confirming impact: are customers seeing 429s or degraded latency?

support-maya: Triton reported increased 429s from their integrations. Support ticket 54321 has logs attached. They say batch job kicked off around 11:02 UTC.

eng-raj: From runtime traces, KV cache hit rates dropped and tail latency spiked; many requests are long-context generation. We should consider temporary RL bump + tighten per-route concurrency for heavy generation path.

sre-jen: Proposed mitigation steps: 1) Apply org-level emergency rate-limit bump to prevent dropped connections 2) Add short-lived per-route caps for /v1/generate-heavy 3) Enable request sampling for debugging. Who can run the org RL change?

oncall-ryan: I can run it. Plan: set org QPS from 200 -> 350 for 20 minutes, monitor error rate. If error rate improves, scale down to 250, then open postmortem.

eng-raj: Suggested command (internal):
```
# emergency override
POST https://controlplane.redwood.internal/v1/orgs/triton-labs/overrides
Authorization: Bearer $INCIDENT_TOKEN
{
  "override":"rate_limit",
  "qps":350,
  "duration_minutes":20,
  "reason":"urgent spike from batch jobs, mitigate 429s"
}
```

oncall-ryan: Running now. tagging ops-bot for audit log.

ops-bot: Audit: user=oncall-ryan action=org.rate_override org=triton-labs qps=350 duration=20m ts=6151234582

oncall-ryan: Done. Patch applied. Monitoring...

sre-jen: Initial telemetry: 1 minute after change, 429 rate dropped 70%, latency p95 down to 420ms. Good sign. Keep an eye on GPU pool saturation.

eng-raj: GPU util on the dedicated pool for region-us-west is at 86%, memory pressure okay. Recommend enabling short-term concurrency limit on /v1/generate-heavy to 3 per org to protect tails. Command: `redwoodctl routes patch --route /v1/generate-heavy --org triton-labs --concurrency 3`

support-maya: I've messaged Triton via support ticket that we're applying temporary changes to stabilize. They asked what the rollback plan is.

oncall-ryan: Rollback plan: after 20m cooldown if error rate < 0.5% maintain qps=250 and keep concurrency cap. If errors spike again, revert to qps=200 and open infra escalation. I'll update the incident channel and page infra if needed.

product-lin: Heads up for downstream teams: this may affect throughput for large-batch ingestion. We'll coordinate with Triton for graceful backoff in their job.

eng-raj: Added request sampling toggle for 2% of traffic for deeper traces: `feature.toggle sampling.triton 0.02`

oncall-ryan: Marking incident status: mitigated (temporary override applied). I'll create follow-up runbook item: investigate why batch job caused such poor cache behavior and add autoscaling rule for heavy-gen pool.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-3742, severity=high, status=mitigated (temporary override). Pagerduty: connected.

support-maya: Closing loop with Triton confirmed via ticket: initial feedback 'latency much improved, thank you'. They will reschedule heavy job.

sre-jen: Postmortem owners: @eng-raj (root cause and runtime fix), @product-lin (coord with customer to prevent recurrence), @oncall-ryan (mitigation verification). Please add notes and timeline to the incident doc.

oncall-ryan: Will draft timeline and commands used. Also will add the override ID from audit for compliance.

eng-raj: Quick note for follow-up: consider adding guardrail to detect 'single-customer burst' and auto-apply per-route concurrency caps before raising org-wide qps.

ops-bot: Audit: incident INC-2026-3742 closed-mitigation ts=6151234920

sre-jen: Thanks everyone. :party-parrot:
